observations.B01: Ink page number is 30: two lobes followed by a closed oval.
observations.B02: Both elevated marks contain a vertical stroke and a distinct dot, so they are exclamation exponents. Both X and M carry hats. Small bottom-edge fragments from the following line are excluded.
observations.B03: The four s subscripts are 0, 1, infinity and lambda. The first t subscript is reinforced and resembles 1 or 4; it is not silently determined from the following 2,3,4. A tiny lower-edge fragment is excluded.
observations.B04: The word dessus is traversed by a single horizontal cancellation; sur follows uncancelled. The repeated large looped group glyph is read as fraktur S. Upper-edge adjacent-line remnants are excluded.
observations.B05: The X and M both have hats and elevated exclamation marks with dots; the arrow points right. The verb reads échangeant. A descender from the prior line intrudes at the top and is excluded.
observations.B06: Between du and coup the manuscript has two horizontal strokes, retained literally as an equals sign. A lower-edge hat fragment belongs to the next line and is excluded.
observations.B07: multiplicités is written above a long cancelled word. That lower word has a tall l and dotted i but its initial letters are obscured, so relations/solutions remains doubtful.
observations.B08: The upper crop boundary clips accent material. Hat fragments survive over both M occurrences; the hat on X is not fully contained, and its presence is therefore left explicitly uncertain in the crop reading. Lower-edge adjacent-line fragments are excluded.
observations.B09: Reference reads 76. The final word begins numéri- and is cut at the right edge, so numérique remains marked unsure. A small upper-edge descender is excluded.
observations.B10: The left reference has a 7 followed by a small crossed/looped numeral, favored 8 but not fully certain. The table has codim 0 and codim 1 headers, one dot labeled 4, a right arrow labeled 1, and an edge between two dots each labeled 2. The brace and table rules are reproduced.
observations.B11: The abbreviation has a descending p and a small elevated ts group; it is not expanded to points. A small upper-edge neighboring descender is excluded.
observations.B12: A hat and dotted exclamation exponent are clear on M. The words read permutés transitivement entre eux. Upper-edge neighboring-line descenders are excluded.
observations.B13: The group glyph has the same double curl as above and a clear subscript 4; a full stop follows. A small upper-edge fragment is excluded.
observations.B14: The first M has no surviving hat and has an elevated ! followed by an. Each chi has a low exclamation. Beneath g and nu, short paired vertical strokes lead to 0 and 3 respectively; these are retained as vertical annotations. Neighboring-line fragments at the top and bottom are excluded.
observations.B15: Hat on M, exclamation exponent, and an are distinct; the projective-space letter is doubled, followed by elevated 1 and an. Adjacent-line fragments are excluded.
observations.B16: Dense hatching above the first M obscures the cancelled decoration; a former hat is only tentative. The U in the middle argument is reinforced or overwritten and remains unsure. The final argument visibly removes {-bar j,-j} and {1/2,2,-1}. Upper/lower edge fragments from neighboring formula lines are excluded.
observations.B17: The first set contains minus bar-j and minus j. The next set reads 1/2,2,-1. The right crop edge reaches the last group symbol but does not show a final closing parenthesis; none is supplied. Upper-edge fragments from the preceding formula are excluded.
observations.B18: The line visibly reads -1+1/3+1/2. The final denominator has a left 2 and right 4 with a crossed curved remnant between them, tentatively an earlier 6. The apparent replacement by 24 is preserved without changing the preceding arithmetic.
observations.B19: NB is underlined. The marginal text reads On peut écrire directement, followed by chi-exclamation of U with an, a division colon, bracketed S_4, and -1/24.
